title: Internal Hom commutes with integral coefficient inversion for general-lfp inputs
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ be finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Put $B=p_X^*\underline R$ and $S=p_X^*\underline E$ on the small pro-étale site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves and ambient relative derived tensor and internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For $M\in D(B)$ write $M_E=S\otimes_B^L M$. Let $K\in D(B)$ have bounded cohomology constructible in the general ring-object sense [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]: each cohomology sheaf admits a finite constructible locally closed stratification on whose strata it is pro-étale locally a cokernel $B^m\to B^n$ with arbitrary local matrix entries and finite $m,n$. Let $L\in D(B)$ have cohomology zero in sufficiently negative degrees; no constructibility or completeness is assumed for $L$.

The canonical evaluation-transpose map
$$S\otimes_B^L R\mathcal Hom_B(K,L)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_S(K_E,L_E)$$
is an isomorphism, natural in both inputs. With the coefficient identification $S=B[1/\ell]$ and its repeated-$\ell$ module telescope [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], its restriction to $D(B)$ agrees with
$$\varinjlim_n R\mathcal Hom_B(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_B(K,\varinjlim_n L),$$
where both sequential transitions are multiplication by $\ell$ and the colimits are exact termwise sheaf-module colimits of complex representatives [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. More precisely, on the $n$th telescope stage the pairing defining the comparison sends $(h,k)$ to $\ell^{-n}(1\otimes h(k))$. The assertion concerns this canonical map, independently of representatives, and the ordinary ambient derived category, without passing to a completed category.

proof.text: First check the topological hypothesis needed for internal continuity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] to the given locally Noetherian, quasi-compact scheme $X$. In a descending chain $(Z_n)$ of closed subsets, choose a minimal member $Z_N$ of the nonempty set of its members. For $n\ge N$, $Z_n\subseteq Z_N$, so minimality forces $Z_n=Z_N$. Thus the underlying space of $X$ is Noetherian.

For each nonzero cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$ apply (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison], with $A=R$. Its input is exactly the finite constructible stratification and the arbitrary-entry local finite presentation in the hypothesis. It gives finite constant scalar local models for $H^q(K)$, allowing a different stratification for each $q$. Since only finitely many $q$ occur, $K$ has bounded constructible cohomology in the finite constant local model sense. No torsion-freeness or completeness of these cohomology sheaves is required.

source.place: Theorem 6.2(2)–(3), Theorem 4.13; use the existing coefficient-specific general-lfp comparison obligation, not merely the heart characterization

proof.text: Use the small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ specified by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], filtered colimits of $B$-module sheaves are exact. Apply [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity] with $\Lambda=\underline R$, using steps 1–2. In particular take any sequential diagram $(M_n^\bullet)$ with a common termwise lower bound; the natural-number category is small and filtered. The evaluation-induced map $\varinjlim_n R\mathcal Hom_B(K,M_n)\to R\mathcal Hom_B(K,\varinjlim_n M_n)$ is an isomorphism. This proves precisely the sequential-continuity hypothesis of the formal localization theorem.

proof.text: Here is an explicit bounded-below representative for the telescope of $L$. Choose $c$ with $H^q(L)=0$ for $q<c$ and any complex $C$ representing $L$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $P^q=0$ for $q<c$, $P^c=\operatorname{coker}(d_C^{c-1})$, and $P^q=C^q$ for $q>c$, with induced differentials. The quotient $C\to P$ induces the identity on cohomology in degrees $q\ge c$, while both sides have zero cohomology below $c$. It is a quasi-isomorphism. Multiplication by $\ell$ descends to $P$, so the repeated-$\ell$ tower has one common termwise lower bound. This construction uses no condition on $L$ beyond the stipulated cohomological lower bound.

proof.text: By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], the actual coefficient map $B\to S$ identifies $S$ with $B[1/\ell]$, with underlying module the repeated-$\ell$ telescope. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-hom-localization-comparison] with ring sheaf $B$, section $s=\ell$, first input $K$, and second input $L$. Smallness, exact filtered colimits and sequential continuity were checked in step 3, and $L$ is cohomologically bounded below. This yields the asserted isomorphism in $D(S)$ for the canonical evaluation-transpose map. The same theorem identifies its restriction to $D(B)$ with the evaluation-induced sequential-continuity isomorphism. It also supplies naturality in both inputs.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), pp. 61–62; agent internal-sheaf localization extraction

proof.text: Pin down the legs of that identification. By [lem-sfb-derived-scalar-localization-reflection], localization is exact termwise extension with unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-complex-colimit] with scalar ring $R$, $t=\ell$, sheaf ring $B$, to $P$ and to any complex representing $H=R\mathcal Hom_B(K,L)$. It identifies each scalar telescope with the restricted localization, with $n$th leg $x\mapsto\ell^{-n}(1\otimes x)$. For a functorial K-injective Hom representative the transition obtained from $\ell_P$ need not literally equal multiplication by $\ell$ on the chain level. The leg-compatible isomorphism of [lem-sfb-kinjective-hom-scalar-telescope] identifies those two colimits and preserves every derived leg. Consequently the preceding restricted comparison is the one between the two scalar repeated-$\ell$ telescopes, including at every stage. No lower bound on the complex representing $H$ is needed.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), pp. 61–62; agent internal-sheaf localization extraction

proof.text: The evaluation normalization of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] identifies the restricted target with $R\mathcal Hom_B(K,L_E)$ by precomposing restricted evaluation with $K\to K_E$. On telescope stage $n$, step 6 gives the leg $h\mapsto\ell^{-n}(1\otimes h)$. Pairing it with $k$ therefore gives $\ell^{-n}(1\otimes h(k))$ by scalar linearity of evaluation. This notation means the corresponding composite of evaluation, the scalar unit, and multiplication by $\ell^{-n}$ on representatives. The next-stage representative is $\ell h$, and $\ell^{-(n+1)}(1\otimes(\ell h)(k))=\ell^{-n}(1\otimes h(k))$, so these pairings form the required cocone. The scalar-adjunction normalization shows that its transpose is exactly the map of step 5. Thus the formula characterizes the canonical derived map, and all choices disappear under the representative-independent continuity and localization isomorphisms already used.
